_note: Blender job kinds (DECISIONS B74, docs/BLENDER-PIPELINE.md 'Jobs'). A job is {model, steps: [{kind, ...params}]} run by tools/blender/jobs.mjs on the shipped model in client/assets/slice/models/. Each kind lists its params: type int|number|bool|string|strings|map|color, with min/max (numbers, list lengths, string lengths) and req. targets: which models it applies to (character = a rigged model folder, prop = props/<name>.glb). A new kind is an entry here plus its handler in jobs.mjs (KIND_RUN).

inspect.what: Print the model: triangles, materials, textures, size, clips (length), bones (parent, rest position in Blender's Z-up armature space, how many vertices each bone moves, the lowest of them). Changes nothing; read it before writing a recipe.

library.what: List the free animation library's clips (Quaternius Universal Animation Library, CC0) with their lengths. Changes nothing.

motion.what: Make walk, run and idle cycles, one-shots (attack, hurt, death: recipe type once) and overlays on existing clips from the model's recipe tools/blender/recipes/<model>.json: feet planted by construction, for four-legged, many-legged and winged bodies. Without clips, every clip and overlay in the recipe.

rigfix.what: Add bones from the recipe's rigfix section and move the mesh's weights onto them (legs the rig lacks, a tail, wings). Every clip the model has keeps playing; the new bones rest until a motion step moves them.

retarget.what: Put clips on a two-legged model that has the shared biped skeleton (the heroes' bone names; a Pixal body rigged by make-model.sh's biped rig has it with its own rest pose), one of: clips, library clips: maps a library clip to {name, loop, sequence (library clips joined in order), inPlace, trim ([from s, to s]), speed (0.25 to 4)}; record the clip's row in docs/ANIMATION-SOURCES.md when it ships. Or from, a two-legged model in the game: every clip of it (hero_gravecaller: the heroes' whole move set, the staff clips too) with each bone's change from rest carried over, so the moves keep the game's timings.

cleanup.what: Fix one clip in place: loop closes the seam, drift removes the body sliding away over the clip, footLock pins feet while they touch the ground (one contact per foot per cycle).

clips.what: Rename clips (rename: {old: new}) or drop clips (drop: [names]). The model's rows follow.

staff.what: Re-bake a discipline hero's staff clips (<clip>_staff, which the game plays while the hero holds a staff: the right arm re-solved so the staff stays upright and leads the casts; tools/blender/recipes/staff.json) from its clips as they are now. Run it after a step that changed one of the recipe's clips, in the same job. Only the recipe's heroes; clips names the plain clips (default: every clip of the recipe).

cloak.what: Stop a two-legged hero's cloak riding up with its body (the shared biped skeleton). arms (default on): the cloth hanging below the arms moves onto copies of the arm bones that follow the arms but never rise more than top degrees (default 20) above the chest's level, so a slam no longer lifts the side panels into a sail. cape (default off; only for a cape that hangs free behind the body, never a robe's skirt): a bone chain down the back cloth that the chest carries but that hangs at most lift degrees (default 10) above its rest, so a deep bow no longer stands the cape up behind (it then hangs from the back instead of following the legs in a walk). With arms down (idle, walk, run) the arms look the same. Later steps that change clips re-key it.

recolor.what: Shift the colour texture: hue (degrees), saturation and brightness (multipliers). only: {color: '#rrggbb', within: 0.05-1} limits it to texels near that colour (soft edge).

decimate.what: Reduce the mesh to about this many triangles (Blender's collapse decimation; skin weights and UVs are kept).

reshape.what: Grow or shrink the part of the mesh a bone moves (and, with children, the bones below it), around the bone's head: a bigger head, longer horns, smaller claws. Best on ends of the body; scale 0.5 to 2.

remove.what: Delete the faces these bones (and, with children, the bones below them) move most: a tail, a horn, a cape. The bones stay.
